newsitem.title: UK: NatWest drops sharply after CEO replacement.
newsitem.headline: NatWest drops sharply after CEO replacement.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc dropped on Monday, after the bank announced its pre-tax profit for the first half year would not exceed 770 million stg, and said it would replace Martin Owen as chief executive at NatWest Markets.
By 1310 GMT, the stock was down to 776-1/2p, retreating from its high of 821p. The shares were at 810-1/2p just prior to the announcement.
"This has been clearly a profit warning", one trader said. In 1996, NatWest's pre-tax profit rose to 879 million stg before exceptional items, up from 714 million stg a year before.

NatWest said it would also review ways of speeding up progress in key areas at NatWest Markets, the investment bank arm of the bank. It said it would invest in those investment banking areas where better return could be achieved.
Group chief executive Derek Wanless was named acting chief executive of NatWest Markets after Owen's departure, NatWest said.
Wanless said NatWest Markets should have a strong leadership, a clear strategy, the best people and a robust control environment.

Dealers said Owen's departure was not a surprise given recent press comment on a re-focusing within NatWest Markets. "That's probably the least surprising element of this statement, given the recent press comment," said the head of equity trading at a large brokerage.
He said NatWest shares should recover as long as the bank was able to convince investors that it was focusing on its more profitable areas.
Yet others said the statement suggested a degree of confusion within the bank over its strategic objectives.
"What surprises me is that 12 or 18 months after they started pumping money into this area they should seem to be having second thoughts," said another dealer.
"It doesn't really smack of a long-term commitment."
-- Christian Gutlederer and David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
